$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages are generated from this directory and are never edited. Google Ads publishes a v25 discovery document, so the callable surface and response shape are checked against Google's machine-readable source.
title: Google Ads

authorize.$comment: Google Ads requires the OAuth bearer AND the developer-token header on ordinary calls. developerToken identifies the installed API application; loginCustomerId selects the manager account only when access to a client is through that manager. An absent optional manager id omits the header rather than sending it empty.

oauth.$grantComment: ONE consent grant shared by every Google connector (MOIC #1, 2026-11-08). A host may run them all on one OAuth client: request each feature's scopes when it is first used, with include_granted_scopes=true, and Google's new token covers every scope granted before. A refresh token comes back only on the FIRST code exchange with access_type=offline, so keep the stored one when an exchange returns none. Revoking ANY token removes the person's WHOLE grant -- every Google connector, not this one -- so a per-feature disconnect stops using the scope locally and only a full Google disconnect revokes. Identify the account by the id_token's sub (request openid; verify iss and aud = clientId), never by email.
oauth.$restrictedScopesComment: Google's RESTRICTED tier puts the whole OAuth client under verification and an annual CASA assessment. None of this connector's scopes is restricted.
oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Google returns a reusable refresh token for offline access. Refreshing replaces the one-hour access token; Google does not document a new refresh token on every refresh response, so the original remains the connection credential until revoked.
oauth.$scopeComment: The v25 discovery method and Google's REST authorization guide both name exactly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords. Google classifies it as restricted, so production OAuth verification is an operational prerequisite.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. Google Ads test accounts live in a separate test-manager hierarchy and cannot interact with production accounts. They appear cancelled, have no billing, never serve ads and produce no serving metrics. The same API host is used, while the connected account decides the estate.
sandboxNote: Use a dedicated Google Ads test manager and test client account. Test and production hierarchies cannot interact; test ads never serve or incur cost, but some features such as billing, conversion uploads and serving reports cannot be exercised there.
$baseUrlComment: v25 is pinned in each request path. It was released 2026-07-22 and is supported until August 2027, buying roughly a year of explicit compatibility. v25.1 was still upcoming when researched; pinning an unreleased revision would make every call fail rather than extend support.
summary: Read Google Ads accounts from a workflow or a Laravel app.
$setupComment: Steps read from Google's docs on 2026-11-14 (each cites its page). Every Google connector shares one grant, so the first four steps are the same for all of them; do them once.

setup.title: Create (or reuse) the Google Cloud project for {{appName}}
setup.detail: Every Google connector shares ONE consent grant (oauth.grant "google"), so use one project and one OAuth client for all of them: one consent and one refresh token per person.

setup.title: Enable the Google Ads API
setup.detail: Console: APIs & Services, Library; open the Google Ads API and click Enable.

setup.title: Configure the consent screen
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Branding (app name {{appName}}, support email, contact email), then Audience: Internal for people inside your Google Workspace organisation only, or External (while it is in testing, add each tester under Test users). Then Data Access, Add or Remove Scopes, and add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords` beside the scopes of any other Google connector you use. You cannot remove the consent screen once it is configured.

setup.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Clients, Create Client; type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs click Add URI and paste {{oauthRedirectUrl}}, then Create. Copy the client ID and client secret when the client is created.

setup.title: Get Google Ads API access and the developer token
setup.detail: Developer tokens are no longer issued from the Google Ads API Center: do not sign up there. Apply from the Google Ads API Overview page in Cloud Console. Access now belongs to the Cloud PROJECT: a new project has Test access (test accounts only, 15,000 operations a day); Explorer access is usually approved automatically (up to 2,880 operations a day on production accounts); Basic and Standard need brand verification first. A production call from an unapproved project fails with CLOUD_PROJECT_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_PRODUCTION.

setup.title: Connect an account and check it works
setup.detail: Connect one Google account through {{appName}}'s OAuth flow, then run the check below.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection, run customer_list_accessible and report the customer ids it returns.
setup.done: customer_list_accessible lists the accounts this Google user can reach.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: The Google Cloud OAuth client shared by the installation.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: The matching Google Cloud OAuth client secret.

credentialFields.label: Developer token
credentialFields.help: The Google Ads API developer token, applied for on the Google Ads API Overview page in Cloud Console (no longer the Ads API Center; access levels now belong to the Cloud project). Google says to treat it like a password; one token identifies the installed application.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: The connected Google user's one-hour OAuth access token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: The reusable offline token used to replace expired access tokens.

credentialFields.label: Manager customer ID
credentialFields.help: Optional. The manager account's 10-digit customer ID without hyphens. Required when the OAuth user reaches a client through that manager; omit it for direct access.
